author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read GitLab audit events, which GitLab Ultimate streams as JSON to an HTTP destination, one event per POST. The destination points straight at a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest URL with two custom headers, so no bridge is needed. Sign-ins, failed sign-ins and user_access_locked go to Auth, and every other event goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- GitLab Ultimate streams audit events as JSON to an HTTP destination, one event per POST, for an instance (Self-Managed, Dedicated) or a top-level group (also GitLab SaaS).
- Point the destination at a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest URL and add two custom headers: Authorization set to Bearer and the integration key, and Content-Type set to application/json, since GitLab sends application/x-www-form-urlencoded by default.
- No bridge is needed.

Field mapping:
- Sign-ins (authenticated_with_*), failed sign-ins (login_failed_with_*_authentication, omniauth_login_failed) and user_access_locked go to Auth; every other event (Git operations, file reads, members, tokens, settings, streaming changes) goes to CloudAudit with the event type as the event name and the entity type as the event type.
- Git fetches and clones, and repository file reads, are data events; everything else is a management event.
- The details object has no fixed schema, so the parsers read only author_class, custom_message (text, or the Git operation object), change, from and to from it.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow GitLab's streamed audit event schema and examples with made-up values.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (126 of 126 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (126 of 126 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these events.
- On 2026-10-16 the parent's confirm string was tightened to ask for author_id and entity_path as well as entity_type and event_type, so other JSON with those two keys, such as Appgate SDP's entity records, isn't claimed.
- In Run Test the parent took every GitLab line in 3 of 3 runs and an Appgate entity record in none.

Known gaps:
- GitLab can send an event more than once, and HTTP Ingest keeps both, so count by sensor_event_id (the event id).
